result.keywords: Service-oriented systems increasingly depend on dynamic discovery, recommendation, and composition of distributed web services, yet varying quality of service metrics can degrade overall user satisfaction. This article examines how deep learning and nature-inspired optimization can be combined to support QoS-aware service recommendation and adaptive composition in volatile environments. The proposed framework integrates collaborative filtering signals with attention-based feature extraction and evolutionary search to rank candidate services, estimate composite QoS, and mitigate sparsity and cold-start issues. Experimental discussion highlights hybrid modeling, scalability considerations, and practical challenges in selecting component services under changing workload conditions.
result.title: Hybrid QoS-aware deep learning framework for adaptive service recommendation and composition
